from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Boundary and Initial Conditions", [
            "PDEs describe infinite possible states.",
            "Initial conditions define the system at start.",
            "Boundary conditions constrain the edges."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        axis = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axis, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Initial condition (a wave)
        initial_curve = axis.plot(lambda x: 1 + 0.5 * np.sin(np.pi * x / 4), x_range=[0, 4])
        self.place_at_grid(initial_curve, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Boundaries (markers at ends)
        b1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        b2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        boundary_points = VGroup(b1, b2)
        self.place_at_grid(boundary_points, 'E2', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(axis))
        self.play(Create(boundary_points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(initial_curve.set_color("#FF00FF")))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(
            Indicate(b1, color="#00FF00"),
            Indicate(b2, color="#00FF00")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-world Impact", [
            "We combine variables, operators, and constraints.",
            "PDEs predict complex natural phenomena.",
            "They drive weather and digital effects."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Recap ODEs to PDEs transition
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        v_label = Text("Variables", font_size=24).set_color(BLUE)
        o_label = Text("Operators", font_size=24).set_color(GREEN)
        c_label = Text("Constraints", font_size=24).set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(o_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(c_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(v_label), FadeIn(o_label), FadeIn(c_label))
        
        arrows = VGroup(
            Arrow(v_label.get_right(), o_label.get_left(), buff=0.1),
            Arrow(o_label.get_bottom(), c_label.get_top(), buff=0.1)
        )
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Summarize Heat and Wave equations visual behavior
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
        
        thermometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thermometer.svg", color=RED)
        wave_line = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(thermometer, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_line, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(thermometer), FadeIn(wave_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Real-world examples: weather and effects
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        speaker_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speaker.svg", color=WHITE)
        pixel_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.1, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3) for _ in range(9)])
        pixel_grid.arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(speaker_icon, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(pixel_grid, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speaker_icon), FadeIn(pixel_grid))
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
sections.content: Briefly review Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) as a 'single-path' relationship. Introduce PDEs as systems with multiple independent variables (space and time). Use an animation showing a line evolving vs. a 2D surface morphing.
sections.example: Comparing a swinging pendulum (ODE - time only) to the vibration of a drum skin (PDE - time and 2D surface coordinates).

sections.title: The Heat Equation: Diffusion in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the Heat Equation as the fundamental PDE for spatial change. Explain the 'concavity' concept—heat flows from hot spots to cold spots. Use a thermal gradient color map animation.
sections.example: A cat sleeping on a cold floor; the heat transfer from the cat's body to the floor tiles over time.

sections.title: The Wave Equation: Ripples and Rhythm
sections.content: Focus on the second-order partial derivative with respect to time. Visualize how a local disturbance (a poke) triggers a wave propagation. Emphasize that speed depends on the medium.
sections.example: A robotic arm striking a guitar string; the animation shows the wave packet traveling back and forth along the string.

sections.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions: Defining the System
sections.content: Explain that PDEs describe 'infinite' possibilities. We need Initial Conditions (snapshot at t=0) and Boundary Conditions (what happens at the edges) to pin down a specific solution.
sections.example: Simulating the water level in an aquarium (PDE) based on the shape of the tank (Boundary) and the initial splash (Initial).

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Impact
sections.content: Synthesize the logic: Variables -> Operators -> Constraints -> Solution. Conclude with how PDEs power weather forecasting and movie special effects.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'fire simulation' in a video game, where PDEs calculate the spread of flames across a 3D environment.
